building.name: Building Code of the City of Tulsa, Oklahoma (Tulsa Revised Ordinances, Title 51, Chapter 1): ICC International Building Code, 2018 Edition, with Tulsa amendments
building.edition: 2018 (the Tulsa amendments in Title 51, Section 101 carry Oklahoma's 2018-edition amendments, marked 'eff 9-14-2021', and add the city's own)
building.local_amendments_note: Section 101 amends the administrative chapter (title, scope, enforcement agency, annual permits, who may apply, fees) and many technical sections. In the chapters that matter for toilet partitions it changes only Section 2902.4.1 (directional signs to public toilets, the state's own 2018 amendment). It does not amend Section 105.2 (work exempt from permit), Table 2902.1, Sections 2902.1 to 2902.3, Chapter 8 (interior finishes) or Chapter 11 (accessibility). Tulsa also adopts the 2018 International Existing Building Code as an optional code (Title 51, Chapter 4).
building.effective_note: The 2018-edition ordinance was on the City Council agenda of May 18 and May 25, 2022 with an emergency clause (council file 22-450); the signed ordinance, its number and its publication date were not read. A January 2026 council ordinance (file 26-39) still titles the chapter 'ICC International Building Code, 2018 Edition, Adopted', and the city's Plans Review page, read 2026-11-24, says 'Tulsa has adopted the 2018 ICC (International Code Council) codes'.
building.quote: Section 100. - Adoption of the ICC International Building Code, 2018 Edition. A certain document, three (3) copies of which are on file in the office of the City Clerk of the City of Tulsa, Oklahoma, being marked and designated as the ICC International Building Code, 2018 Edition, as published by the International Code Council, Inc., hereinafter the "Building Code" is hereby adopted for the control of buildings and structures other than detached one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses, as herein provided. Each and all of the regulations, provisions, penalties, terms and conditions of the ICC International Building Code, 2018 Edition, are hereby referred to, adopted and made a part hereof as if fully set out in this chapter with the amendments thereto, prescribed in Section 101 of this chapter.

fixtures.basis: Tulsa's amendments to the 2018 International Building Code (Title 51, Section 101) and to the 2018 International Plumbing Code (Title 56, Section 101) were read in full in the council packets. Neither touches the toilet-count table (Table 2902.1 / Table 403.1), the half-and-half split and rounding (2902.1.1), the small-occupancy exceptions (2902.2) or the urinal share (424.2). The only Chapter 29 / Chapter 4 fixture amendment is the directional-sign rule the state itself added in 2021. Tulsa's table is therefore the 2018 model table, not the 2024 one in the state pack; the rows for offices, restaurants and schools and the urinal share were read on the 2018 copy and are the same figures as the state pack's, so the state pack's worked examples stand.
fixtures.quote: 2902.4.1 Directional signage - Amendatory. Directional signage indicating the route to the required public toilet facilities in Group A, B, I, M, and R-1 occupancies shall be posted in a lobby, corridor, aisle, or similar space, such that the sign can be readily seen from the main entrance to the building or tenant space. Only one sign at each main entrance that is intended for public use shall be required. [...] [Source: Added at 38 Ok Reg 2573, eff 9-14-2021]

table_2018.split: 2902.1.1: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. [...] Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 2902.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number.
table_2018.separate: 2902.2 Separate Facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: Separate facilities shall not be required for dwelling units and sleeping units. Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.
table_2018.urinals: 424.2 Substitution for Water Closets. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.

restrooms_city.rule: City policy (Joint Administrative Order 2006-04, listed on the Plans Review page among current 'Building Code Policies' for Section 2902.2): on the applicant's request and with the code official's approval, one unisex toilet facility may replace separate men's and women's facilities in business, factory, high-hazard, storage and utility occupancies with a maximum occupant load of 49 or less, if the owner files a 'Notice of Unisex Toilet Fixture' on the property abstract. No Tulsa ordinance on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms was found. The 2018 code Tulsa's ordinance adopts requires single-user rooms to be 'identified for use by either sex' and has no provision for a shared multi-user all-gender room (the 2024 state code has).
restrooms_city.quote: UNISEX TOILET FIXTURE. Subject to the request of the applicant and approval of the code official, a single unisex toilet facility may be permitted in lieu of separate facilities required by IBC 2003 Section 2902.2 (IPC 2003 Section 403.2), in B, F, H, S, and U occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 49 or less. This approval is contingent upon the property owner filing a "Notice of Unisex Toilet Fixture" document (attached) on the property abstract generally indicating the provided toilet fixtures are not in compliance with the Tulsa Building Code, Title 51 of the Tulsa Revised Ordinances. The "Notice of Unisex Toilet Fixture" document form will be provided for the property owner by the City of Tulsa.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Tulsa job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the rules Tulsa's Permit Center applies.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Tulsa office towers, aerospace and manufacturing plants, schools and event venues, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law sets the sizes, and Tulsa's building rules add a national accessibility standard on top. The city checks access with the building permit.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Tulsa's building rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The city's own amendments don't change the counts. The table below shows what that means.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Beyond the federal rules:** under the 2018 rules in Tulsa's ordinances, the side wall next to the toilet needs an 18 inch vertical grab bar as well as the horizontal one, which the federal rules don't ask for. Oklahoma's 2024 rules add two more things. The front partition and one side partition of the wheelchair stall need 12 inches of clear space above the floor, where the federal rule asks for 9. A new building's restroom needs a 67 inch turning circle, where the federal rule asks for 60.
page.code_change_bullet: - **New rules expected on January 1, 2027:** Tulsa's ordinances still adopt the 2018 editions of the national model codes, with city amendments. Oklahoma made the 2024 editions the statewide minimum on September 14, 2026. The city says its update to the 2024 editions is in progress, with a pending adoption date of January 1, 2027, and that plans submitted after it adopts them must meet the new codes. Ask the Permit Center which edition applies to your project.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked for use by either sex. Under the 2018 rules in Tulsa's ordinances, a building needs separate men's and women's rooms unless it holds 15 people or fewer (25 for an office, 100 for a store). By city policy, an office, factory, warehouse or storage building that holds 49 people or fewer may have one restroom open to everyone instead, if the owner asks, the code official approves and the owner files a notice on the property record. Oklahoma's 2024 rules allow a shared all-gender room if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and every urinal has privacy partitions. Tulsa's 2018 rules don't provide for one, so ask Development Services before planning it. Oklahoma law requires shared restrooms in public schools, from pre-kindergarten to 12th grade, and in state correctional facilities to be designated for one sex.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** the City of Tulsa's Development Services department issues building permits. The city's list of work that needs no permit includes painting, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work, and movable fixtures, counters and partitions that are not fixed in place and stand no taller than 5 feet 9 inches. The list doesn't name toilet partitions. The city says a permit is typically needed to build, remodel, move or repair walls, floors, ceilings, windows or doors. Ask the Permit Center (918-596-9456) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Tulsa Development Services Permit Center
page.stalls_intro: Tulsa's rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal needs a screen on each side.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building. The counts are the same under the 2018 rules in Tulsa's ordinances and the 2024 rules Oklahoma adopted in September 2026. An office with 25 people or fewer, a store with 100 or fewer, or any other space with 15 or fewer doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: Tulsa's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.install_rule: Tulsa's Permit Center takes a Contractor Registration form from installers, and only a licensed tradesperson may apply for trade permits. Oklahoma has no state license for general construction or most specialty installers. The state licenses plumbing, electrical, mechanical and roofing work only. Confirm with the City of Tulsa Development Services Permit Center. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Oklahoma has no state license for this kind of work, and Tulsa's Permit Center takes a Contractor Registration form from installers.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Oklahoma has no state wage law for public jobs, so a set wage applies only on federally funded projects, under federal law. For a carpenter on building work in Tulsa County that rate is $14.96 an hour plus $1.55 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.517% in Tulsa: 4.5% state, 3.65% city and 0.367% Tulsa County.
page.buyers_extra: - **Arenas, convention halls and event venues:** long runs of stalls with heavy-duty hardware, in a material that takes crowds and nightly cleaning.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Building Code of the City of Tulsa (Tulsa Revised Ordinances, Title 51, Chapter 1: ICC International Building Code, 2018 Edition, with Tulsa amendments, which references ICC A117.1-2009) and Plumbing Code of the City of Tulsa (Title 56: ICC International Plumbing Code, 2018 Edition, with Tulsa amendments), both before the City Council in May 2022; 2024 International Building Code and 2024 International Plumbing Code with Oklahoma amendments (OAC 748:20-2 and 748:20-16, with ICC A117.1-2017), the statewide minimum since September 14, 2026, with Tulsa's adoption pending for January 1, 2027; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: which edition Tulsa's plan reviewers apply today. The city's ordinances and Plans Review page name the 2018 codes; Oklahoma's 2024 codes have been the statewide minimum since September 14, 2026; the city gives January 1, 2027 as a pending adoption date (Permit Center, 918-596-9456).
